blocks.text: Re: Engagement for an investor relations program
Dear Lauren:

Thank you for the conversations that led to this letter, and for the candor with which you and your colleagues described where the company's investor communications stand today. This letter confirms the terms on which Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC ("Ashcombe," "we," or "us") will support {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} (the "Company") in building and running an investor relations program. We have tried to set those terms out plainly, so that both of us can refer back to them with confidence as the work proceeds.
Scope of the engagement

Our work will concentrate on how the Company presents itself to the investment community, and on how consistently it does so from one setting to the next. Specifically, we expect to review the Company's current shareholder base and analyst coverage, conduct confidential perception interviews with a selection of investors and analysts, and work with management to develop a clear and durable investment narrative.

Building on that work, we will help the Company put in place the calendar, presentation materials, and approval practices that a lasting program requires, including support around its quarterly results. We will also advise on outreach to investors who do not currently hold the Company's shares but who, in our judgment, should come to understand its story. We will agree with you at the outset which of these elements matter most, and we will weight our time accordingly.
How we will work together

Much of our work is done by correspondence: we draft, route materials for your review, and keep a clear record of what has been approved and by whom. We will hold working sessions with your team at intervals we agree together, and we will report progress to you in writing between them.

Nothing we prepare will be released to any outside party without the Company's prior approval. The Company retains sole responsibility for the accuracy and completeness of its public statements and for compliance with applicable securities laws and any listing requirements. This engagement does not include legal advice or the preparation of regulatory filings; where those are needed, we will coordinate with your counsel.
What we will ask of the Company

To do this work well, we will need timely access to the Company's recent results materials, shareholder records, and any investor feedback it has already gathered, together with reasonable access to members of management. We will keep our requests focused, and we will route them through you unless you direct otherwise.
The Ashcombe team

Michael Morris, a Partner of the firm, will lead the engagement day to day and will be your principal point of contact. He will be supported by Laura Bradley, Senior Associate, who will manage drafts, version control, and the approval record for each item, and by Michelle Black, Communications Analyst, who will lead our research on the shareholder register, peer companies, and media and analyst coverage.

I will remain involved throughout, reviewing material before it reaches the Company and joining working sessions where that is useful. We would ask that you serve as the Company's lead contact for the engagement, so that every approval has a single and reliable route. Should a change in staffing become necessary, we will discuss it with you in advance, and we will not reassign a senior member of the team without your agreement.
Commencement and fee

We propose that our work commence on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}, with a kickoff session for your team shortly after that date. We anticipate that the program will run for approximately nine months, and our fixed professional fee for the scope described in this letter is {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}}.
Fees and payment

We will invoice the fixed fee in installments over the term of the engagement, on a schedule we will confirm with you at kickoff, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of receipt. Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, such as travel for investor meetings, will be billed at cost and incurred only with the Company's prior approval.
Term and termination

This engagement will continue until the work described above is complete, unless it is ended earlier by either party. Either of us may terminate the engagement on thirty days' written notice, in which case the Company will pay the portion of the fee attributable to work performed, together with approved expenses incurred, through the effective date of termination.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence all non-public information the Company shares with us, use it solely for the purposes of this engagement, and limit access to those members of our team who need it. We recognize that some of this information may be material and non-public, and our team will observe any trading restrictions and blackout periods the Company notifies to us. These obligations will survive the end of the engagement.
Other clients

We advise a number of companies, and from time to time some of them may operate in markets related to the Company's. We will not act for another client on a matter directly adverse to the Company while this engagement continues, and we will raise with you promptly any situation that could reasonably be seen as a conflict.
Limitation of liability

Our advice is intended to assist management, which retains responsibility for all decisions taken and public statements made by the Company. Except in the case of our gross negligence or willful misconduct, our aggregate liability arising from this engagement will not exceed the fees paid to us under this letter, and neither party will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential losses.
Governing law

This letter and any matter arising from it will be governed by the laws of the state in which Ashcombe maintains its principal office, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. Should any disagreement arise, we would ask that it first be raised directly between you and me, so that we have the opportunity to resolve it together.
Acceptance

We are glad to be working with you and your colleagues, and we look forward to the program ahead. If this letter reflects your understanding, please sign below and return a copy to me; on receipt, Michael will be in touch to schedule the kickoff session with your team.
Sincerely,
Kickoff Memo: Investor Relations Program for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}

To: Laura Bradley, Michelle Black
From: Michael Morris
Re: Objectives, division of the work, and the first assignments
What we have been asked to deliver

Our engagement with {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} formally began on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}, and its purpose is to build an investor relations program the company can eventually run on its own, with Lauren Heath, the Chief Operating Officer, as our sponsor and the single route through which every approval will pass. Over roughly nine months the company should come away with three things: a narrative its management can deliver the same way in every setting, an accurate picture of who owns the stock today and who ought to, and a calendar, set of materials, and approval routine that keep working after we step back.
How the work divides
The work falls into four strands, and although they overlap, each has one of us responsible for it so that Lauren always knows whom to ask:

items: Shareholder and coverage baseline, led by Michelle Black: the current register, how ownership has moved over the last couple of years, and which analysts cover the company or have stopped covering it, so that we know who we are talking to before we decide what to say.

Perception interviews, led by Laura Bradley with Michelle Black: confidential conversations with a selection of holders and analysts, conducted in the company's name with its approval and written up without attribution.
Investment narrative, led by me with Laura Bradley: the core account of the business that management gives, drafted with Lauren Heath and then tested against what the interviews tell us.

Calendar, materials, and approvals, led by Laura Bradley: the quarterly results routine, the investor presentation, the investor section of the website, and a written process for who signs off on what before anything goes out.

blocks.text: The strands are not equal in weight at the start: for the first month most of our time will go into the baseline and the interviews, because the narrative depends on both, and the calendar and materials strand will mostly wait until we have something worth putting into a presentation.
The order of the first assignments

The first working session with Lauren is not fixed yet, so for the next few weeks the sequence matters more than the calendar, and I would like us to work in this order: (1) Laura sends Lauren our information request this week, asking for the latest shareholder register or ownership report, the past year of results materials, and any investor feedback the company has collected itself; (2) Michelle starts the baseline from public filings and published coverage while we wait for the register, so that nobody is idle; (3) Laura drafts the interview guide and a proposed list of interviewees, which Lauren has to approve because we will be calling people on the company's behalf; and (4) I draft a first outline of the narrative from what we already have, on the understanding that the interviews will change it.
Versions and approvals

Lauren will be routing our drafts to her management colleagues, which means a superseded version reaching the company would cost us more than it usually does. Laura Bradley owns the version labels and the approval log for this engagement, so please send anything bound for the client through her, and copy me on any message that asks the company to approve something. Laura will also keep a running list of open items for Lauren, which I will review before each weekly status note goes to the client.

If anything here does not match what you have heard from Lauren Heath in our conversations so far, tell me before the information request goes out, since that request is the first document the company will see from this team.
Hi Lauren,

We are a few weeks into the program now, so I am starting this thread as the one place for status and approvals on the {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} work, which should mean you have a single message to answer instead of several separate ones from Laura, Michelle and me. I have attached version 3 of the kickoff memo, which includes the changes you asked for to the order of the work and to who leads each part.

On progress, Michelle has finished a first pass at the shareholder and analyst baseline from public sources, Laura has a draft interview guide ready for you that follows the structure we discussed, and I have a rough outline of the narrative that I am holding back until the interviews give us something to test it against. Michelle's work already points to a few gaps in the register that are worth discussing, and I would like to go through those with you once the transfer agent's data lets us confirm them.

To keep the interviews on schedule, could you send us (1) the most recent shareholder register or ownership report from your transfer agent, since the public filings only show part of the picture, and (2) your approval of the proposed interviewee list Laura sent last week, with any names you would like added or removed? Once we have both, Laura will start booking the first conversations.

Sincerely,
Michael
Investor Relations Program: {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}
Briefing for Lauren Heath and the management team, prepared by Michael Morris with Laura Bradley and Michelle Black. Program under way since {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}.
What the interviews are telling us

items: Holders who know the company well credit management with steady execution, but few could explain how the parts of the business fit together
Analysts want results explained the same way every quarter, particularly margins and capital spending
Several investors hear from the company only around results and would welcome contact between quarters
No one raised concerns about governance or disclosure; the gaps are in clarity and frequency of contact

blocks.text: The register and the coverage

items: Ownership sits mainly with a small group of long-term holders, which brings stability but limits trading liquidity
Funds that own comparable companies are largely missing from the register, and they are the natural first targets for outreach
Analyst coverage is thinner than at peers of similar size, so each published note carries more weight with holders
Michelle Black's peer benchmarking shows where the company's disclosure is lighter than the peer group's

blocks.text: Draft investment narrative

items: A plain statement of what the company does and where it earns its returns, written in management's own words
A small number of themes, each supported only by figures the company has already disclosed
One agreed way of describing margins and capital spending, used on every call and in every presentation
Draft is with Lauren Heath for comment now and will be revised once the remaining interviews are written up

blocks.text: Who does what

items: Michael Morris: program lead and first call on anything time-sensitive
Laura Bradley: drafts, version control, and the approval log for every item
Michelle Black: register analysis, peer benchmarking, and coverage monitoring
Weekly status by email to Lauren Heath, and a working session with the full team about once a month

blocks.text: What we need from management before the next session

items: Comments on the draft narrative from Lauren Heath and her colleagues, so the revision can start as soon as the interviews close
Approval to approach the target funds once the narrative is settled
A view on whether the program should include a non-deal roadshow or a dedicated investor event
A date for the next working session, ahead of the next results call

blocks.text: Working Session Minutes: Investor Relations Program, {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}
A working session at about the halfway point of the program. Notes taken by Michelle Black. Our thanks to Lauren for making the time at a busy point in the quarter.
Present

items: Lauren Heath, Chief Operating Officer, {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}
Michael Morris, Partner
Laura Bradley, Senior Associate
Michelle Black, Communications Analyst (notes)

blocks.text: Interview findings

Laura confirmed that the perception interviews are complete. The written summary went to Lauren without attribution, as we agreed at the start. Lauren said the findings match what she hears informally from holders. We will fold the remaining points into the narrative.
The narrative

Mike opened with the revised investment narrative. Lauren had shared it with her management colleagues before the session. Their comments were about emphasis, not substance. We were glad to hear it, because the structure has held up well through the interviews.

Margins took most of the discussion. Lauren asked that we use one description of margins everywhere, including the results script and the investor presentation. Everyone agreed. Laura Bradley will carry the change through each draft so the versions stay in step.
Capital spending came up briefly. Lauren would like it described alongside margins, not on a page of its own. Mike agreed and will reflect that in the next draft.
Outreach to new investors

Laura took us through the targeting shortlist. It is made up of funds that own comparable companies but not this one. Lauren is comfortable with us approaching them once the narrative is final. She asked that nothing go out before management has rehearsed it. We think that is the right order, too. I will prepare a short profile of each fund so management knows who they will be meeting.
Website and materials

We spent a few minutes on the investor section of the website. Lauren agreed it should carry the same narrative as the presentation. Laura will send a marked-up version of the current pages. Nothing changes on the site until management has rehearsed the new language.
Results preparation

The next results call will be the first real test of the narrative. Mike will draft the script and a set of likely questions. He and Laura will then run a rehearsal with management. Lauren will find a time that suits her team.
Coverage

I shared the latest coverage summary. Nothing in recent coverage needs a response from the company. One recent analyst note repeated the older margin framing, which supports the change Lauren asked for. We will watch for it again after results.

Status Report: Investor Relations Program for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}
Prepared by Michael Morris, with Laura Bradley and Michelle Black, for the management team of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}.
Where the program stands

We are at about the halfway point of the program, and the work has moved from research into use, which is the shift we planned for when the engagement began: the perception interviews are complete, the investment narrative is agreed in draft, and management has rehearsed it and used the new margin language in public on the most recent results call.

The interviews confirmed what the early baseline suggested, that holders who know the company well trust its management but want the business explained the same way every quarter, and nearly all of the work since the last report has been aimed at closing that gap.

The main work still ahead is outreach to investors who do not yet own the stock, together with the calendar and approval routine that the company will keep running after we finish, and both are on track to begin this month.

Since the last report the team has closed out the following items, listed in the order they were finished:

blocks.text: Planned for the coming period

The narrative is now stable enough to take outside the company, so the next period is about putting it in front of new investors while keeping existing holders informed, and over the coming weeks we expect to: (1) begin approaches to the shortlisted funds, starting with those that already own several of the companies in Michelle Black's peer benchmarking; (2) finish the investor presentation and the investor section of the website so that both carry the agreed narrative in the same words where it matters; (3) put the written approval routine in front of management for sign-off, so that every external document has a named approver; and (4) offer the covering analysts a short briefing with management between quarters, which the interviews told us they would value.

Michael Morris remains the first contact for anything time-sensitive during this period, and the weekly status note will continue to go out on the usual day, with Laura Bradley's list of open items attached.
Budget

The engagement budget is the fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}} set out in the engagement letter, and the work completed to date sits within the share of that fee we planned for the first half of the program. The remaining work is covered by the same fee, and out-of-pocket expenses so far have been limited to items management approved in advance.

If the company decides to add a non-deal roadshow or a dedicated investor event, the travel and venue costs would be billed as expenses outside the fee, and we would set them out for approval before committing to anything.
Risks and open decisions
Most of the risk at this stage concerns consistency and timing, not content, and each item below is set out with what we propose to do about it:

rows: Different speakers describing the business in different terms
Analysts compare what they hear on calls with what they hear in meetings, and a gap undercuts the narrative
A one-page message sheet for each member of management who speaks to investors, and a review of every presentation before it is given
Outreach starting before management is ready
A first meeting with a new fund is hard to repeat if it goes poorly
Approaches begin only after management has signed off the narrative and the presentation
Decision on a roadshow or investor event
Either needs several weeks of lead time and an expense decision
A decision from management at the next working session
Thin analyst coverage
With few published views, any single note carries more weight with holders
Continued monitoring by Michelle Black, and the between-quarter briefings described above

blocks.text: The one decision we need from management before the next report is whether to include a roadshow or investor event in the second half, because that choice sets the calendar for most of what follows, and Laura Bradley will circulate a short note on the options this week so that the discussion can be brief.
